report.TASK: GK3: GK1's five SQL statements and the ledger child, first run, on a throwaway database.
WORKS: No SQL defect and no defect in the ledger child: nothing in the SQL file, the manifest or the child
was changed.
First run on a database with the schema of before GK1 and two existing rows: the five statements
each completed (three ALTER TABLE, CREATE TABLE, CREATE INDEX) in one query call. 12 columns,
7 constraints and 2 indexes were added, nothing was removed or changed, and the budget row and
the call row stayed, with the new columns empty.
Second run: no-ops, not refusals. Each of the five answered 'already exists, skipping'; tables,
columns, constraints, indexes and row counts are identical (same catalogue hash).
The server's migrate() and scripts/platform/demo-schema.ts, once each after that: both ran, nothing
changed.
sql.test.ts on that database: 8 of 8 pass, 0 skipped. The test skipped until now runs.
The ledger child ran every owner step: key-marks, reconcile, restore-key; exit 0 with names, states
and times only, and exit 1 with the gateway's own closed message for a changed price.
A ledger pinned to one key refuses a hold under a list policy (MODEL_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED) until
reconcile; after it the first key serves. The same after a fourth key joined the list.
A cited 429 through the ledger's own retainExposure() closed the call at zero and marked the first
key; the second key became in_use; restore-key put the first back.
The officer provider reads a key whose value is empty as absent and names it.
The container was removed by its exact name; containers, volumes and networks are the same before
and after, by name.
SEE_IT: (creates one container ulpin-gk3-sqltest-<8 hex>, removes it, about 40 seconds)
E:/BhuAayam-data/task-data/gk3/run-1.json: the run's full record (every column, constraint, index)
INPUTS: The image compose.yaml:15 pins by digest (already local, nothing pulled).
The gateway file and the manifest of commit 63c986d5 from Git; the file as it is now (sha256 in
A synthetic policy (project gk3-control) and four synthetic keys generated in the run.
GAPS: The two existing rows were synthetic and the tables small. How long the ALTER TABLE on
usp_model_calls holds its lock on the demo's real rows was not measured; it adds one empty column
No statement failed, so what a failure halfway leaves behind was not observed. The file is one
query call, which PostgreSQL runs as one transaction; that is its documented behaviour, not a
Each statement's result was read through the same text and the same driver call that
migrateModelGateway() makes, because the function itself discards the results. The function ran
third (inside migrate()) and fourth (demo-schema.ts), both as no-ops.
The base schema came from the server's producers in the manifest's order; migrateUsp() has no entry
that stops before its later steps, so those were applied too. None touches the gateway's tables.
sql.test.ts now also accepts a throwaway container named by its runner. The old form (run-sql.mjs's
container) was not run again: run-sql.mjs refuses this machine's Docker endpoint.
demo-gateway.mjs itself (the command line around the child) was not run: it reads the demo
settings. The child was started with the same arguments it uses.
A pinned producer source changed (officer-ai-provider.ts); docs/api was not regenerated.
DESIGN: The container keeps the task's name; the test got a second accepted form instead of a second name.
It now reads only labels and published ports from Docker, never the container's environment,
because this container holds a password there.
The URL carries no password: the pg driver reads PGPASSWORD from the child's environment.
The runner records a child's output only when it holds neither the password nor a synthetic key.
The base database was pinned as one key, so the run shows the real roll-out step: one key to a list.
